DONE — analysis executed end-to-end. Headline answer below; tables, robustness and caveats follow.

HYPOTHESIS (deliverable text, also in results/hypothesis.md):
In this NLSY79 cohort-sequential sample, the FAMILY net wealth (respondent/spouse unit — the only wealth construct in the file) of white respondents (operationalised as `Racial/ethnic cohort, 1979 == 3`, NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC) exceeded that of black (`1:BLACK`) and Hispanic (`2:HISPANIC`) respondents in every wave from 1985 onward, and the disparity widened sharply over the eleven years. Unweighted complete-case medians (nominal-year $): 1985 — white $3,500 (n=5,774), black $1,600 (n=1,699), Hispanic $500 (n=2,631); 1990 — $12,972 (5,336), $4,800 (1,528), $1,600 (2,431); 1996 — $42,600 (3,557), $9,800 (1,368), $2,562.50 (2,114). Both the ratio AND the absolute dollar gap widen, in the same direction: white:black 2.19x → 2.70x → 4.35x (bootstrap 95% CI 1985 [1.84, 2.47] vs 1996 [3.68, 5.25], non-overlapping) and white:Hispanic 7.00x → 8.11x → 16.62x ([5.80, 8.75] vs [13.73, 21.75]), while the dollar gaps grew from $1,900 / $3,000 to $32,800 / $40,038. The widening survives the balanced-panel (n=5,739: 2.38→3.60→4.69 and 12.67→12.29→17.75), p99 winsorising (numerically unchanged — the supplied wealth variables are already top-coded near p99), and CPI adjustment (within-wave ratios are invariant; real W:B gap $2,771 → $32,800). Real medians grew for all three cohorts (black x4.20, Hispanic x3.52, white x8.35), so this is about relative rates of accumulation over early adulthood, not absolute decline. The shortfall is distribution-wide but largest at/below the median (1996 ratios 4.35/16.62 at p50, 2.52/6.55 at p75, 2.10/4.39 at p90) and is mirrored by zero-or-negative net wealth in 1996 (black 20.8%, Hispanic 34.9%, white 10.9%). Secondary composition check (blank = "owned none", an assumption): by 1996 black respondents' observed asset means had nearly converged on white levels (residential $40,191 / 36.8% owning vs $44,902 / 37.4%; vehicles $7,010 vs $7,178) despite a 4.35x lower median net wealth, implying the residual gap is carried by liabilities and by financial assets absent from the file; the Hispanic gap additionally reflects far lower homeownership (23.5% vs 37.4%). Statements are scoped to this unweighted sample (no weights in the file; Sample IDs map 1:1 to race cohorts and cannot identify military subsamples, so no exclusions were made); no causal interpretation.

payload.hypothesis: From 1985 onward, white (NLSY79 cohort 3, NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC) respondents' family net wealth exceeded that of black (cohort 1) and Hispanic (cohort 2) respondents in every wave, and both the ratio and the absolute dollar gap widened: median family net wealth was $3,500 white vs $1,600 black and $500 Hispanic in 1985 (ratios 2.19x and 7.00x; gaps $1,900 and $3,000), $12,972 vs $4,800 and $1,600 in 1990 (2.70x, 8.11x; $8,172, $11,372), and $42,600 vs $9,800 and $2,562.50 in 1996 (4.35x, 16.62x; $32,800, $40,038) - nominal dollars, unweighted complete case. Real (CPI-adjusted) medians grew for all three cohorts (x4.20 black, x3.52 Hispanic, x8.35 white), so the divergence is relative: white median family wealth grew about twice as fast. The widening holds in the balanced panel (W:B 2.38->4.69; W:H 12.67->17.75), after p99 winsorising (unchanged; source already top-coded near p99) and in constant 1996 dollars, so it is not an outlier or 1996-attrition artefact. It is largest at and below the median (1996 white:cohort ratios 4.35/16.62 at p50 vs 2.10/4.39 at p90; zero-or-negative net wealth in 1996: 20.8% black, 34.9% Hispanic, 10.9% white). Secondary composition evidence indicates by 1996 black respondents' observed assets (residential, vehicles, items over $500) nearly matched white levels while median net wealth remained 4.35x lower, implying debts and unobserved financial assets carry the residual gap, whereas the Hispanic gap also reflects much lower homeownership (23.5% vs 37.4%). Scope: this cohort-sequential, unweighted NLSY79 sample, family/spouse-unit wealth, no causal claim.
payload.workflow: 1) Read data/nls_raw.csv as strings; verified empty string is the only missing code, no sentinel values, all non-blank wealth values numeric-parseable; 2) coerced wealth, cohort and 12 asset-component columns to numeric; 3) coverage/value-range audit (blanks 20.4/26.7/44.5%; negatives and zeros retained as legitimate; top-coding detected); 4) HEADLINE: unweighted complete-case median family net wealth per wave per cohort with means, p25/p75/p90, share<=0 and 1000-rep bootstrap CIs; 5) white:black and white:hispanic median ratios (2000-rep bootstrap CIs) plus absolute dollar gaps; 6) quantile ratios (p50/p75/p90) to locate the gap in the distribution; 7) ROBUSTNESS 1: balanced panel observed in all three waves (n=5,739) - medians, ratios, gaps; 8) ROBUSTNESS 2: p99 winsorised medians/ratios; 9) SENSITIVITY: constant-1996-dollar medians via external CPI-U and nominal vs real 1985->1996 growth multiples; 10) SECONDARY: composition decomposition under the blank->0 assumption with ownership rates and owners-only means, plus zero-filled means relative to the white-cohort mean; 11) descriptive Sample-ID table (no exclusions) and attrition diagnostics; 12) independent re-computation of medians/ratios with the stdlib csv module as a cross-check. All tables printed with cohort labels and year in the columns.
